description: Default parameters of the transporter_switch stage (C21) for rat and mouse hippocampus and neocortex: chloride reversal potential of GABA-A / glycine receptors moves from depolarising (NKCC1, high internal chloride) to hyperpolarising (KCC2) during the first postnatal weeks. Values are defaults for a Param, not fitted data; results are 'in this simulation'.
citations: Zhang et al. 2006, J Neurophysiol 95:2404-2416 (mouse retina)
Tyzio et al. 2008, Eur J Neurosci 27:2515-2528 (rat hippocampus)

observations.immature: high NKCC1, [Cl-]i about 25-40 mM, E_Cl about -50 to -40 mV (above a rest of -65 to -70 mV): GABA depolarises
observations.mature: KCC2, [Cl-]i about 4-14 mM, E_GABA about -75 mV (rat hippocampus) to -60 mV (retina): GABA hyperpolarises (see provenance_notes)
observations.timing: NKCC1-dominated from E12 to about P4; functional switch between P5 and P10 (hippocampus and neocortex), up to P12-P14 in superficial layers
observations.mechanism: onset programmed by age, timing accelerated by activity (GABA depolarisation -> Ca2+ -> BDNF / TrkB -> KCC2)

age_unit: days of postnatal age (P0 = 0); give `age` (or `now` and a clock in days) in this unit
notes: midpoint 7.5 d and width 1.25 d put 10-90 % of the switch between about P4.8 and P10.2 (sigmoid 10-90 % = midpoint +/- 2.2 width), i.e. the P5-P10 window; activity_gain 0 is purely programmed (no gain value is given by the sources).

observations.immature.quantity: intracellular chloride, E_Cl and E_GABA of immature neurons
observations.immature.note: About 30 mM in P0-P3 rat Cajal-Retzius cells and 29 mM in mouse retina before P6; E_Cl -39 mV and E_GABA -45 mV in the retina. The 40 mM upper end and cortical E_Cl values were not found in the accessible text.

observations.mature.quantity: E_GABA (not E_Cl) and intracellular chloride of mature neurons
observations.mature.region: CA3 pyramidal somata; retinal ganglion and amacrine cells
observations.mature.note: Read by an assistant in a browser session on 2026-11-04. E_GABA about -75 mV and [Cl-]i about 4 mM in adult CA3 (their bicarbonate-corrected E_Cl is about -82 mV); retina after P6 about -60 mV and 14 mM (5-20 mM). Ben-Ari 2002 gives -75 mV as a resting potential, and Rivera et al. 1999 gives neither 4-5 mM nor -75 mV (driving force of GABA-A about -10 mV).

observations.timing.quantity: ages of the NKCC1 period and of the GABA switch
observations.timing.note: The direction (first postnatal week depolarising, switch near P6 in retina, KCC2 rising P1-P14, later maturation of younger neurons) is supported; the exact E12-P4, P5-P10 and P12-P14 windows were not found in the accessible text.

observations.mechanism.quantity: activity-dependent control of the GABA switch
observations.mechanism.note: Only BDNF raising KCC2 expression and GABA itself promoting the switch are supported; the TrkB step, the Ca2+ link and activity-accelerated timing were not verified.

params.e_mature.region: hippocampal CA3 pyramidal somata (applied by default to neocortex and retina)
params.e_mature.note: Mouse retina after P6 gives about -60 mV. Using the CA3 value for other regions is a model choice; set another value for a region you have data for. It asserts 10 mV of hyperpolarising drive over v_rest = -65 mV.

params.midpoint.method: Centre of the P5-P10 window for the functional switch; the exact window is not stated in the accessible text.

params.width.quantity: width of the sigmoid of the switch (days)
params.width.method: The sigmoid's 10-90% span (midpoint +/- 2.2 * width) set to about P4.8-P10.2, i.e. the P5-P10 window.

params.activity_gain.quantity: acceleration of the switch by activity
params.activity_gain.note: No gain value is given by the sources; 0 means purely programmed timing.

params.v_rest.quantity: resting potential used to turn E_GABA into a driving force (mV)
params.v_rest.note: The original profile quotes -65 to -70 mV for immature neurons without a source; Ben-Ari 2002 gives about -75 mV at any age.

params.receptors.quantity: receptor classes switched by the stage
params.receptors.note: A modelling choice (GABA-A and glycine receptors share the chloride switch).
